text:
emily: heads up - customer reported mass SCIM provisioning 429/503s after we rolled the RBAC flattening change yesterday. also seeing intermittent SAML login failures and KMS decrypt errors in identity-provisioner logs. anyone on call?

ajay: on it. which tenant and can you paste the prov logs snippet?

emily: tenant: acme-corp-prod. snippet from identity-provisioner: 
```
2026-03-20T22:11:04Z identity-provisioner ERROR kms: decrypt failed: kms:plaintext-not-found
2026-03-20T22:11:05Z scim PATCH 503 tenant=acme-corp-prod body_len=4230 id=usr_8f3...
2026-03-20T22:11:06Z auth-proxy WARN saml: assertion length=4128 groups=482
```
used to be ~1.2kb assertions.

sam: ok — RBAC flatten likely expanded group list in assertion. okta and our gateways sometimes trip when assertion + headers get big. kms plaintext-not-found suggests alias/key mismatch post-rotation. did we rotate KMS last night?

maria: i rotated the identity-provisioner key at 2026-03-20T21:50 as part of scheduled rotation. i started a re-encrypt backfill but it error'd on some records due to role-propagation TTL on the worker. i'm checking the journal now.

emily: we need triage fast, customer is in active SLO alerts. quick actions i'm doing: 1) revert provisioner to previous image (rolled) 2) enable verbose kms and scim logs 3) notified support. please coordinate escalations here.

ajay: pls grab one redacted successful and one failed assertion (headers + saml xml) and drop here — redact emails/IDs. also run: `kubectl logs -n identity identity-provisioner-0 --since=10m | sed -n '1,200p'` and paste any KMS stack traces.

maria: journal shows rotation was 2-stage: created new key, updated alias, queued re-encrypt job. re-encrypt worker failed on ~4k items because the worker's IAM role assumed cache had stale policy for kms:Decrypt. role propagation TTL ~5m. we retried but backlog coincided with RBAC push, so a lot of records attempted decrypt with old alias mapping.

sam: action plan proposal: A) pause SCIM retry loops to stop 429 flood (prevent downstream overload) B) promote re-encrypt backfill job to high priority C) patch provisioner to treat KMS NotFound as retriable-with-alias-lookup and fall back to alias history mapping D) if unstable in 30m, rollback the RBAC flattening.

emily: doing A now (paused retry queue). sam take B/C. maria if we need D please be ready to trigger. i'll update customer and prod SRE.

deploy-bot: deployment started: identity-provisioner v2.14 -> rollback to v2.13 requested by emily

sam: quick note — auth-proxy logs showed `saml: assertion exceeded maxLen` earlier, so we should also trim group attributes short-term. easiest mitigations: send group_count only, or compress group list into hashed group ids until we finish RBAC normalization.

maria: re-encrypt backfill now running with higher qps, ETA ~12m. KMS failures dropped from ~60/min to ~3/min after bumping worker IAM propagation and retry logic.

emily: customer reports improved login success rates. retaining paused retries for another 10m then will resume slowly. will write a postmortem with timeline, root cause (race between KMS rotation + RBAC flatten creating large assertions + re-encrypt backlog + role-propagation TTL), and remediation (alias-history fallback, safer rotation cadence, assertion size guardrails). :thumbsup:

ajay: thanks team — also filing a vuln-triage ticket to check whether assertion size expansion could be abused for header-truncation attacks; tagging infra-security.

sam: i'll open a PR for the fallback logic and a small auth-proxy change to cap assertion attr size.

emily: awesome. leaving watch on logs for next 30m and will follow up with incident channel.
